study.title: Calcific patellar tendinopathy, one case: multimodal care with ultrasound tracking, cause unknown
study.evidence_note: Single case report. Multimodal package, no control. Isometrics used only in weeks 1–2, dose not given. Indirect to mid-portion Achilles.
study.confidence_note: Free full text read via publisher pages. NPRS, LEFS, GROC values only in figures, not read. Supplement with isometric dose not opened.
study.impact_line: One squatter improved with a kitchen-sink package. Says nothing about isometrics or Achilles; don't change your plan.
key_findings: 46-year-old lifter, 6 wk of calcific patellar tendon pain, improved with a 4-part package
Package: spinal and lower-limb manipulation, ultrasound-guided electro-dry needling, BFR, progressive loading
Isometrics used in weeks 1–2 only; exercise, hold and sets not reported in the main text
Pain-free jogging, jumping and squatting by 3 mo; 215 lb squat pain-free at 11 mo
Calcific foci looked fewer and smaller on ultrasound; never measured
summary: Case report from American Academy of Manipulative Therapy clinicians, US direct-access practice
Ultrasound used to diagnose, guide needling and track the tendon over 11 months
NPRS and LEFS said to beat their MCIDs from early on; values shown only in graphs
Can't separate the effect of any single component from natural history
Barely addresses isometrics: named as a phase, no dose given
study.bottom_line: A single uncontrolled case of calcific patellar tendinopathy improving with manipulation, dry needling, BFR and loading. It can't show what worked, and it tells you nothing about isometric dosing for early mid-portion Achilles pain.

design: No registration or ethics approval stated
participants: 6 wk left anterior knee pain after more squat volume
Ultrasound: calcific foci at inferior pole, hypertrophy, partial-thickness tear
intervention: 2x/wk for 12 wk, then 2x/month boosters for 6 mo
Every session: HVLA thrust to cervical, thoracic, lumbar, hip and talocrural
Wk 2–12: US-guided fenestration (2 needles, 3x30 s), then electro-needling 20 min, 2 Hz
Wk 1–2: isometric tendon loading, pain ≤4/10; dose not in main text
Wk 3–6: BFR at 80% LOP, 3x15 to failure, RPE 7–9
Wk 7–12: hip and knee strengthening; plyometrics once quads symmetry >90%
primary_outcome: NPRS, LEFS, GROC, 10RM knee extension, ultrasound appearance

results.result: From 7/10; authors report ≥2-point drop by wk 3
results.detail: Follow-up values appear only in Figure 3, which wasn't readable in the text extract, so no numbers are given here.

results.result: From 50/80; above MCID at every follow-up
results.detail: Follow-up values appear only in Figure 4; not read. GROC is in Figure 5 only.

Table 3, left/right lb: baseline 20/80, 6 wk 60/80, 3 mo 70/85, 6 mo 75/90, 11 mo 80/90. Symmetry percentages derived, not stated. Plyometrics began at 12 wk citing >90% symmetry, but the 3-mo 10RM was 82%.

results.result: Pain-free jog, jump, squat, stairs at 3 mo; 215 lb squat at 11 mo
results.detail: Baseline 1RM squat not possible because of pain. Her goal was a barbell squat over 135 lb.

results.result: Fewer, smaller foci; more fibrillar; still thickened
results.detail: No counts or sizes given; 'significantly smaller' is a visual impression, not a test. Long-axis only, no Power Doppler, assessor and blinding not reported. Sonopalpation painless at every follow-up.

key_numbers.label: Uncontrolled case, four treatments at once

pico.p: One 46-year-old woman, strength trainer, 6 weeks of calcific patellar tendinopathy
pico.i: Manipulation, ultrasound-guided electro-dry needling, isometrics then BFR then progressive loading and plyometrics
pico.o: NPRS, LEFS, GROC, 10RM knee extension, ultrasound appearance to 11 months

limits: Four treatments at once; no component can be credited
Natural history and regression to the mean not excluded
Pain and function values in graphs only
Ultrasound change judged by eye, long-axis only; blinding not reported

full_text.why: Read in full from the free full text (publisher HTML and PDF via WebFetch). Figures 3–5 values and Supplemental File 2 (treatment plan incl. isometric dose) not accessed; PMC page blocked by captcha.

how_to_apply: Don't change your early mid-portion Achilles isometric plan on this paper.
Calcific patellar tendon: keep progressive loading as the backbone.
Use 10RM knee extension side-to-side to track quads recovery.
Gate plyometrics on measured strength symmetry, not time alone.
Don't promise calcific foci will resolve; structure may lag symptoms.
applies_to: Active adults with calcific insertional patellar tendinopathy
Clinicians with ultrasound and dry-needling skills, as hypothesis only
not_for: Choosing isometric dose for any tendinopathy
Showing that manipulation or dry needling helps tendons
Replacing ultrasound-guided lavage or shockwave decisions

domains.reason: Age, sex, activity, goals and history given.

domains.domain: History clearly described and presented as a timeline
domains.reason: Onset clear, but abstract says 18 visits over 24 weeks while methods imply far more.
domains.support: Abstract vs methods schedule (2x/wk 12 wk + boosters)

domains.reason: Pain, aggravating tasks, ROM, strength, LEFS and baseline ultrasound all reported.

domains.domain: Diagnostic tests and results clearly described
domains.reason: Calcification shown on long-axis ultrasound only; no size measured, no Doppler, operator and blinding not stated.
Needling and BFR detailed, but isometric and strengthening doses not in main text.
domains.support: Intervention section; Table 2; dose deferred to Supplemental File 2

domains.reason: Strength and goals reported numerically; pain, LEFS, GROC only graphed; ultrasound change qualitative.
No adverse events reported for needling, manipulation or BFR.
Limitations acknowledged, but conclusion promotes the package beyond what one case shows.

grade.reason: Single uncontrolled case, four co-interventions, blinding not reported; can't attribute change to treatment.
Calcific insertional patellar, not mid-portion Achilles; isometrics briefly used, dose unreported.
n = 1; no effect estimate or CI; fails optimal information size entirely.
Successful single cases are preferentially published.

clinical_significance: Authors report NPRS beyond 2-point MCID (Salaffi 2004) and LEFS beyond 9-point MCID (Mehta 2016)
Within-person change only; no between-group effect or NNT possible
Tells you a recovery is possible, not how likely or why
comparator_fairness: Loading alone, the standard, was never tested against the add-ons
alternative_explanations: Natural history: calcific tendinopathy can resorb on its own
Regression to the mean: seen at 6 weeks near peak pain
Progressive loading alone could explain the strength and function gains
High contact time and expectation effects
spin: Conclusion pitches the ultrasound-integrated package as more comprehensive; one case can't show that
Most authors are from an academy training these techniques; no conflict statement
fit_with_evidence: Progressive loading fits patellar tendinopathy reviews and the Atlas tendon playbook
Isometric pain relief is inconsistent in trials; this adds nothing to that question
No trial evidence that manipulation helps tendinopathy
external_validity: ✓ Active adult gym lifter, typical of Curt's caseload
✓ Loading progression and strength gating are usable
✗ Calcific insertional patellar tendon, not mid-portion Achilles
✗ Ultrasound-guided needling and point-of-care scans aren't routine here
would_change_my_mind: An RCT of loading with vs without US-guided needling in calcific tendinopathy
A dosed isometric trial in early mid-portion Achilles pain
Case series with measured calcification size and blinded reads
weaknesses: Isometric dose not in main text
Pain and function values only graphed
Visit count conflicts between abstract and methods
No funding, conflict, ethics or publication-consent statement
appraisal.funding_conflicts: Funding and conflicts not stated. Five authors are affiliated with the American Academy of Manipulative Therapy, which trains manipulation, dry needling and ultrasound; no disclosure given.

disagreements.why: Paper calls it a direct-access case report only.
Imaging section silent on operator and blinding.

disagreements.resolved: Agreed: step reworded; inconsistency noted in result detail.

disagreements.second: weak; Australia is direct access too
disagreements.why: Real gap is guided needling and point-of-care scans.

verification.external_searched: PEDro site search on title terms: none (case reports not indexed). Web search for reviews rating it: none; published Sept 2026. search.pedro.org.au not opened.

study.patient_explanation: One person with a calcium-affected kneecap tendon got back to heavy squatting with a mix of treatments. We can't tell which part helped, or whether it would have settled anyway, so we stick with steady, graded tendon loading.
open_questions: Does US-guided needling add anything to loading for calcific tendinopathy?
What isometric dose, if any, helps early tendon pain?
How often does calcific patellar tendinopathy resorb untreated?
Does calcification size predict recovery time?

sources.citation: Young I, Salzman A, Dunning J, et al. Calcific Patellar Tendinopathy: A Case Report Integrating Diagnostic Ultrasound Throughout a Multi-Modal Treatment Approach. Int J Sports Phys Ther 2026;21(9):879-89.
